sections.heading: Identity and current status
sections.body:
- Project ID: `muse-code`
- Canonical name: Muse Code (`claim-muse-code-sf-identity`)
- Current status: public beta; actively developed (`claim-muse-code-sf-status`)
- Last source-backed identity check: 2026-08-18
- Vendor: Meta Superintelligence Labs (`claim-muse-code-sf-vendor`)
- Canonical URL: `https://developer.meta.com/ai/products/muse-code/` (`claim-muse-code-sf-canonical-url`)
- Repository: unknown; no public repository URL found (`claim-muse-code-sf-repository-url`)
- Availability: macOS and Linux; beta access (`claim-muse-code-sf-availability`)

sections.heading: What it is and is not
sections.body:
- What it is: Meta's terminal-based coding agent on Spark 1.2 with integrated CI execution, co-trained harness architecture, and replay-exact event logging (`claim-muse-code-sf-unique-value`, `claim-muse-code-sf-identity`)
- What it is not: not OpenClaw (which uses Muse Glimmer model), not a provider wrapper around API endpoints, not generally available yet (`claim-muse-code-sf-not-for`)

sections.heading: Architecture and agent-loop ownership
sections.body:
- Primary type: `runtime` is a catalogue taxonomy inference from co-trained terminal harness owning the agent loop; pages do not use `runtime` as a product-type label (`claim-muse-code-sf-primary-type`)
- Secondary role: `runtime` with CI execution mode (`claim-muse-code-sf-secondary-role`)
- Agent-loop owner: Muse Code owns the agent loop; co-trained harness architecture, not a provider API wrapper (`claim-muse-code-sf-agent-loop-owner`)
- Architecture: local terminal binary plus Meta Model API for Spark 1.2 inference (`claim-muse-code-sf-architecture`)

sections.heading: Orchestration and parallelism
sections.body:

sections.heading: Isolation, permissions, security, and data path
sections.body:
- Isolation: two-layer fail-closed containment — Seatbelt on macOS, bubblewrap on Linux. Sandbox on by default. `--yolo` flag drops guards. Hooks and MCP run unsandboxed when enabled (`claim-muse-code-sf-isolation`, `claim-muse-code-sf-tag-sandbox`, `claim-muse-code-sf-yolo-flag`)
- Permissions: gated approval system; `--yolo` bypasses approval (`claim-muse-code-sf-permissions`)
- Security: two-layer fail-closed sandbox; replay-exact event log; `--yolo` flag removes guards (`claim-muse-code-sf-security`)
- Data path: unknown exact on-disk location

sections.heading: Pricing, license, maintenance, and lock-in
sections.body:
- Pricing: no Muse Code seat SKU. Spark token pricing — Standard: $1.25 input / $0.15 cached / $4.25 output per 1M tokens; Contributor: $0.10 input / $0.002 cached / $0.20 output per 1M tokens. Contributor trains on data (`claim-muse-code-sf-pricing`)
- License: unknown; no open source license found (`claim-muse-code-sf-license`)
- Maintenance: beta status, actively developed 2026 (`claim-muse-code-sf-maintenance`)
- Lock-in: Meta credential required; Spark API tokens (`claim-muse-code-sf-byok`)

sections.heading: Unique edge, meaningful drawbacks, best fit, and not-for
sections.body:
- Unique edge: co-trained harness not a provider wrapper; two-layer fail-closed containment; replay-exact event log; multi-agent by default; Beta access to Spark 1.2 (`claim-muse-code-sf-unique-value`)
- Meaningful drawbacks: beta status, macOS/Linux only, Meta credential required, Contributor tier trains on data, `--yolo` drops guards, hooks/MCP unsandboxed, concurrency clamp 2-16 vs typical 4-8 can limit parallelism (`claim-muse-code-sf-drawback`)
- Best fit: developers wanting terminal-native coding agent with strong sandboxing on macOS/Linux, comfortable with Meta ecosystem and Spark models (`claim-muse-code-sf-intended-user`)
- Not-for: not for Windows users, not open source, not BYOK (Meta credential required), not generally available yet (`claim-muse-code-sf-not-for`)
